title: Psalm 147 — He counts the number of the stars

verdicts.reasoning: hallĕlû yāh kî-ṭôb zammĕrâ ʾĕlōhênû ...: 'Praise Yah!' keeps imperative and name; 'our Elohim'. MT unit kept against LXX/Vulgate Pss 146-147 division (recorded). Exact.
bônēh yĕrûšālaim YHWH nidḥê yiśrāʾēl yĕkannēs: English name forms (founder point D). Exact.
hārōpēʾ lišbûrê lēb ûmĕḥabbēš lĕʿaṣṣĕbôtām. Exact.
mōneh mispār lakkôkābîm lĕkullām šēmôt yiqrāʾ: ASV 'counts' with NRSV 'determines' recorded; reception note separated. Exact.
gādôl ʾădônênû wĕrab-kōaḥ litbûnātô ʾên mispār: 'our Lord' (title) distinct from YHWH; 'beyond number' keeps the mispār echo. Exact.
mĕʿôdēd ʿănāwîm YHWH mašpîl rĕšāʿîm ʿădê-ʾāreṣ: 'down to the ground'. Exact.
ʿĕnû laYHWH bĕtôdâ zammĕrû lēʾlōhênû bĕkinnôr. Exact.
hamkasseh šāmayim bĕʿābîm hammēkîn lāʾāreṣ māṭār hammaṣmîaḥ hārîm ḥāṣîr: 'skies' (physical). Exact.
nôtēn libhēmâ laḥmāh libnê ʿōrēb ʾăšer yiqrāʾû. Exact.
lōʾ bigbûrat hassûs yeḥpāṣ lōʾ-bĕšôqê hāʾîš yirṣeh: 'the legs of a man'. Exact.
rôṣeh YHWH ʾet-yĕrēʾāyw ʾet-hamyaḥălîm lĕḥasdô: 'kindness' (central chesed-solitary). Changed line verified.
šabbĕḥî yĕrûšālaim ʾet-YHWH hallĕlî ʾĕlōhayik ṣiyyôn: fem. imperatives; 'your Elohim'. Exact.
kî-ḥizzaq bĕrîḥê šĕʿārāyik bērak bānayik bĕqirbēk. Exact.
haśśām-gĕbûlēk šālôm ḥēleb ḥiṭṭîm yaśbîʿēk. Exact.
haššōlēaḥ ʾimrātô ʾāreṣ ...: accusative of direction 'to the earth'; ʾimrâ 'command' distinct from dābār 'word'. Reception note ('telecommunication') kept out of the line. Exact.
hannōtēn šeleg kaṣṣāmer kĕpôr kāʾēper yĕpazzēr. Exact.
mašlîk qarḥô kĕpittîm lipnê qārātô mî yaʿămōd. Exact.
yišlaḥ dĕbārô wĕyamsēm yaššēb rûḥô yizzĕlû-māyim: rûaḥ 'wind'. Exact.
Source checked: Ketiv דברו, Qere דְּבָרָיו; Qere 'his words' translated, ASV Ketiv 'his word' recorded. Exact.
lōʾ ʿāśâ kēn lĕkol-gôy ûmišpāṭîm bal-yĕdāʿûm halĕlû-yāh: MT kept against LXX 'he did not make known'; the resumptive 'his' is declared in commentary. Exact.

glossaryReview.reasoning: Philologically neutral and correctly direct: a typographic convention, with the Hebrew form standing in the source text and every name verified (David, Solomon, Jerusalem, Zion, Israel, Jacob, Job). Flagged only because it is founder point D (the corpus split with the Kings transliteration). Reviewer view: accept English forms for the Writings. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, which are not retro-edited, and the four books must agree with each other. Record the genre split (narrative transliterated, poetry English) as deliberate, or settle it corpus-wide in one later decision.

Every site verified: YHWH; 'Yah' (Ps 147:1, 20); the article follows the Hebrew (anarthrous Ps 8:6; Eccl 3:10, 13; articular Eccl 3:11, 14, 15, 17, 18); 'El', 'Eloah' and 'Shaddai' as in stable job-woh (38:41; 40:2, 9); 'our Lord' for ʾădōnênû. Direct is right: these are presentation rules over explicit Hebrew forms. Flagged only for founder point A (Ps 8:6 'Elohim' against the canon's 'the Elohim'). Reviewer view: keep the anarthrous form. The Hebrew has no article, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and the Kings clause 2, and departing from the canon's wording here is evidence that the line is not canon-driven.

Site-by-site application of the founder's Kings-wave register ruling, checked verse by verse: physical sky 'skies' (Ps 8:2, 4, 9; 19:2, 7; 33:6; 147:8; Prov 8:27; Eccl 3:1; Job 37:3); dwelling or cosmic height 'heavens' (Ps 33:13 || mĕkôn-šibtô; 139:8 against She'ol). Ps 8:2 ('splendor upon the skies') is the closest call and is argued from v 4. Direct is appropriate.

'earth' at universal and cosmic sites (kol-hāʾāreṣ; ʾereṣ || tēbēl) is the reading of ASV, NRSV and NJPS, and the isaiah-woh precedent. 'land' is kept for territory (Prov 10:30; Job 37:13) and the stable 'wings of the land' (Job 37:3 = 38:13). Every site was checked. Agree with founder point C: promote the clause to central eretz in a later diff.

Inferred is the honest class: the traditional English of Eccl 3:21 is 'spirit'. The lexical evidence is real. BDB and HALOT give rûaḥ 'breath (of life)'; NJPS has 'lifebreath' at Eccl 3:21; and vv 19-21 argue about the one rûaḥ that humans and beasts share (Gen 6:17; 7:15, 22). Lower-case 'spirit' at Ps 139:7 follows NRSV and NJPS. 'wind' (Job 37:21; Ps 147:18) and 'breath of his mouth' (Ps 33:6) are uncontroversial.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012)
glossaryReview.reasoning: All six pairs were verified in the Leningrad source (Job 37:12; Ps 139:6, 16; 147:19; Prov 8:17, 35), and all Qere are translated. The ASV-follows-Ketiv statements at Ps 139:16 and 147:19 are correct. No seventh pair exists: Prov 8:16 is a manuscript variant, as the editor says. Direct is correct.

Applied correctly at every listed site. MT Psalm numbering was verified (superscription = v 1 in Pss 8, 19; run into v 1 in Ps 139). The one vowel-only exception at Ps 8:2 is declared and justified: the MT impv. tĕnâ has no syntax after ʾăšer. Eccl 3:21 keeps the Masoretic articular participles and fully records the interrogative reading of LXX, Vulgate, ASV, NRSV and NJPS. Non-blocking: add 'KJV' to the Eccl 3:21 clause as the English witness to the MT pointing ('the spirit of man that goeth upward'), so that the entry does not suggest that every English version departs from the MT.
appliesTo +12 matches appliesToAdded exactly (verified against base); every site carries the ref and follows the register rule.
+12 sites verified. The article follows the Hebrew; the rule is recorded in the overlay, parallel to Kings clause 2.

citations: Sakenfeld, The Meaning of Hesed in the Hebrew Bible (1978)
glossaryReview.reasoning: The extension is correct and the changed lines were verified (Ps 33:5, 18, 22; 147:11; Job 37:13). 'kindness' is lexically defensible for solitary ḥesed (Glueck; Sakenfeld). Flagged for founder point E only, because the Psalter has about 120 further occurrences. Reviewer view: confirm 'kindness' now, before the Psalms grow, so that the rendering does not drift. It is the central wohChoice, it is consistent with genesis-woh and Kings, and the loyalty sense is carried in commentary. 'steadfast love' (NRSV) is the main alternative.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: All 20 lines checked. 147:4-5, 15 render the Hebrew; the astronomy and telecommunication readings stay in notes. No flags.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 205 verses, the 17 overlay entries and the 16 central-diff ops were formed from the chapters, the Leningrad source files, the overlays, the diff, the 2.83.0 base and the canon-quotation file before wave-w1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's list of the three canon-coincident lines (section 1) confirmed the two commentary revisions: at Job 37:18 and Prov 8:30 the notes cite only the canon's French, whose wording matches the line, and omit the canon's English ('the sky'; 'as one brought up with him'), which does not. Prov 8:22 already shows the correct treatment. The report's six-pair Ketiv/Qere count was independently confirmed.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-Ps-8:6-article-on-Elohim: Keep 'a little less than Elohim' without the article. The Hebrew mēʾĕlōhîm is anarthrous, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and Kings clause 2, and the reception note already gives the canon's 'the Elohim'. Differing from the canon here is useful evidence that the line follows the Hebrew.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-bene-(ha)adam: Accept 'the sons of the human' / 'the sons of human' for coherence with central ha-adam / ben-adam and GEN-WOH-11:5, and align 1 Kgs 8:39 ('the children of men') to it. The cost is stiff English at Prov 8:4, 31, and the Hebrew article on bĕnê (hā)ʾādām carries no difference in sense. If the founder prefers idiom, revert every plural site together to 'the sons of men' (string swap; drop the plural refIds from the ha-adam and ben-adam ops). Do not mix the two.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-eretz-cosmic-earth: Agree. Promote the 'earth' scope clause (isaiah-woh + Writings) to central eretz in a dedicated later diff, after the parallel appliesTo merges have landed.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-proper-names: Accept English forms in the four Writings books. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, and the four books must agree. Record the corpus practice as genre-split (narrative transliterated, poetry and prophets English) or settle it in one corpus-wide decision. Do not leave it implicit.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-chesed-kindness: Confirm 'kindness' for solitary ḥesed now, before the Psalter grows (about 120 occurrences). It is the central wohChoice, consistent with genesis-woh and Kings, and lexically sound (Glueck; Sakenfeld). The loyalty sense stays in commentary, and the fixed pair ḥesed wĕʾĕmet stays under chesed-v-emet.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-Job-37:18-clouds: No decision needed: 'clouds' rests on BDB/HALOT, KJV and stable job-woh 38:37, and 'strong' (not 'solid') keeps the line neutral. The reviewer asks for one transparency sentence (JOB-WOH-37:18 revise; shechaqim op revise): the canon's English edition reads 'the sky', so the canon is itself divided.

No lens leakage in any line. Flags are founder-confirmation points (A, B, D, E). Revisions are factual or mechanical. Status awaiting-human.

paragraphs.text: הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ ׀ כִּי־ט֭וֹב זַמְּרָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־נָ֝עִים נָאוָ֥ה תְהִלָּֽה׃

i18n.en: Praise Yah! For it is good to sing praises to our Elohim; for it is pleasant, and praise is fitting.

notes.official: *hallĕlû yāh* 'Praise Yah!' (the MT writes two words here and joins them with maqqef in v 20). *yāh* is the short form of the divine name (Ex 15:2) and is kept as a name, rather than absorbed into 'Hallelujah' or replaced by 'Praise the LORD' (ASV 'Praise ye Jehovah'; `divine-names-convention-writings`). *ʾĕlōhênû* 'our Elohim' (`elohim-as-translation`). *kî-nāʿîm nāʾwâ tĕhillâ* 'for it is pleasant, and praise is fitting' (ASV); some take *nāʿîm* of YHWH ('for he is gracious'). The LXX and the Vulgate divide MT Ps 147 into two psalms (146 = vv 1-11; 147 = vv 12-20); the MT numbering is followed (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`).

paragraphs.text: בּוֹנֵ֣ה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה נִדְחֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל יְכַנֵּֽס׃

i18n.en: YHWH builds up Jerusalem; he gathers together the outcasts of Israel.

notes.official: *bônēh yĕrûšālaim YHWH* 'YHWH builds up Jerusalem'; *nidḥê yiśrāʾēl yĕkannēs* 'he gathers together the outcasts of Israel'. Names are in their English forms, as in job-woh (`proper-names-english-forms-convention-writings`); the Kings overlays transliterate (Yerushalayim, Yisra'el).

paragraphs.text: הָ֭רֹפֵא לִשְׁב֣וּרֵי לֵ֑ב וּ֝מְחַבֵּ֗שׁ לְעַצְּבוֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.

paragraphs.text: מוֹנֶ֣ה מִ֭סְפָּר לַכּוֹכָבִ֑ים לְ֝כֻלָּ֗ם שֵׁמ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽא׃

i18n.en: He counts the number of the stars; he calls them all by names.

notes.official:
*mōneh mispār lakkôkābîm* 'He counts the number of the stars' (ASV 'counteth'). *mnh* also means 'appoint, allot', and NRSV has 'determines the number'; the line keeps the ASV. *lĕkullām šēmôt yiqrāʾ* 'he calls them all by names' (cf. Isa 40:26).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes vv 4-5 ('He telleth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by their names ... his understanding is infinite') to show that astronomy and interplanetary travel were unimaginable at that time. The lines render the Hebrew.

paragraphs.text: גָּד֣וֹל אֲדוֹנֵ֣ינוּ וְרַב־כֹּ֑חַ לִ֝תְבוּנָת֗וֹ אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

i18n.en: Great is our Lord, and mighty in power; his understanding is beyond number.

notes.official: *gādôl ʾădônênû wĕrab-kōaḥ* 'Great is our Lord, and mighty in power': *ʾădōnênû* 'our Lord', the title, kept distinct from YHWH (`divine-names-convention-writings`). *litbûnātô ʾên mispār* 'his understanding is beyond number' repeats the *mispār* of v 4 (ASV 'infinite'). See the reception note at v 4.

paragraphs.text: מְעוֹדֵ֣ד עֲנָוִ֣ים יְהוָ֑ה מַשְׁפִּ֖יל רְשָׁעִ֣ים עֲדֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: YHWH lifts up the humble; he brings the wicked down to the ground.

notes.official: *mĕʿôdēd ʿănāwîm YHWH* 'YHWH lifts up the humble'; *ʿădê-ʾāreṣ* 'down to the ground' (ASV), *ʾereṣ* as the ground (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: עֱנ֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה בְּתוֹדָ֑ה זַמְּר֖וּ לֵאלֹהֵ֣ינוּ בְכִנּֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: Sing to YHWH with thanksgiving; sing praises upon the harp to our Elohim,

notes.official: *ʿĕnû laYHWH bĕtôdâ* 'Sing to YHWH with thanksgiving' (*ʿnh* IV 'sing', perhaps antiphonally); *lēʾlōhênû* 'to our Elohim' (`elohim-as-translation`).

paragraphs.text: הַֽמְכַסֶּ֬ה שָׁמַ֨יִם ׀ בְּעָבִ֗ים הַמֵּכִ֣ין לָאָ֣רֶץ מָטָ֑ר הַמַּצְמִ֖יחַ הָרִ֣ים חָצִֽיר׃

i18n.en: who covers the skies with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass grow on the mountains.

notes.official: *hamkasseh šāmayim bĕʿābîm* 'who covers the skies with clouds': the physical sky, 'skies' (central `shamayim`; ASV 'heavens'). *hammēkîn lāʾāreṣ māṭār* 'who prepares rain for the earth' (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: נוֹתֵ֣ן לִבְהֵמָ֣ה לַחְמָ֑הּ לִבְנֵ֥י עֹ֝רֵ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִקְרָֽאוּ׃

i18n.en: He gives to the beast its food, to the young ravens which cry.

notes.official: *libnê ʿōrēb ʾăšer yiqrāʾû* 'to the young ravens which cry' (cf. Job 38:41).

paragraphs.text: לֹ֤א בִגְבוּרַ֣ת הַסּ֣וּס יֶחְפָּ֑ץ לֹֽא־בְשׁוֹקֵ֖י הָאִ֣ישׁ יִרְצֶֽה׃

i18n.en: He does not delight in the strength of the horse; he takes no pleasure in the legs of a man.

notes.official: *bĕšôqê hāʾîš* 'in the legs of a man', the strength of the runner or the foot soldier, parallel to the horse.

paragraphs.text: רוֹצֶ֣ה יְ֭הוָה אֶת־יְרֵאָ֑יו אֶת־הַֽמְיַחֲלִ֥ים לְחַסְדּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: YHWH takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope for his kindness.

notes.official: *rôṣeh YHWH ʾet-yĕrēʾāyw* 'YHWH takes pleasure in those who fear him'; *lĕḥasdô* 'for his kindness' (central `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness`; ASV 'lovingkindness').

paragraphs.text: שַׁבְּחִ֣י יְ֭רוּשָׁלִַם אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה הַֽלְלִ֖י אֱלֹהַ֣יִךְ צִיּֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: Laud YHWH, Jerusalem; praise your Elohim, Zion.

notes.official: *šabbĕḥî ... hallĕlî* 'Laud ... praise': feminine imperatives addressed to Jerusalem and Zion (`proper-names-english-forms-convention-writings`). *ʾĕlōhayik* 'your Elohim' (`elohim-as-translation`). The LXX begins its Ps 147 here.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־חִ֭זַּק בְּרִיחֵ֣י שְׁעָרָ֑יִךְ בֵּרַ֖ךְ בָּנַ֣יִךְ בְּקִרְבֵּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: For he has strengthened the bars of your gates; he has blessed your children within you.

paragraphs.text: הַשָּׂם־גְּבוּלֵ֥ךְ שָׁל֑וֹם חֵ֥לֶב חִ֝טִּ֗ים יַשְׂבִּיעֵֽךְ׃

i18n.en: He makes peace in your borders; he satisfies you with the finest of the wheat.

notes.official: *haśśām-gĕbûlēk šālôm* 'He makes peace in your borders'; *ḥēleb ḥiṭṭîm* 'the finest of the wheat' (lit. 'the fat of wheat').

paragraphs.text: הַשֹּׁלֵ֣חַ אִמְרָת֣וֹ אָ֑רֶץ עַד־מְ֝הֵרָ֗ה יָר֥וּץ דְּבָרֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: He sends out his command to the earth; his word runs very swiftly.

notes.official:
*haššōlēaḥ ʾimrātô ʾāreṣ* 'He sends out his command to the earth' (accusative of direction; ASV 'upon earth'; `eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`). *ʾimrâ* 'saying, command' (ASV 'commandment') is parallel to *dĕbārô* 'his word', and the line keeps two English words for the two Hebrew words. *ʿad-mĕhērâ yārûṣ dĕbārô* 'his word runs very swiftly'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the verse ('He sendeth forth his commandment upon earth: his word runneth very swiftly') as an allusion to telecommunication, which could not be understood at that time. The line renders the Hebrew.

paragraphs.text: הַנֹּתֵ֣ן שֶׁ֣לֶג כַּצָּ֑מֶר כְּ֝פ֗וֹר כָּאֵ֥פֶר יְפַזֵּֽר׃

i18n.en: He gives snow like wool; he scatters the hoarfrost like ashes.

paragraphs.text: מַשְׁלִ֣יךְ קַֽרְח֣וֹ כְפִתִּ֑ים לִפְנֵ֥י קָ֝רָת֗וֹ מִ֣י יַעֲמֹֽד׃

i18n.en: He casts out his ice like morsels; before his cold who can stand?

notes.official: *mašlîk qarḥô kĕpittîm* 'He casts out his ice like morsels' (hail); *lipnê qārātô mî yaʿămōd* 'before his cold who can stand?'

paragraphs.text: יִשְׁלַ֣ח דְּבָר֣וֹ וְיַמְסֵ֑ם יַשֵּׁ֥ב ר֝וּח֗וֹ יִזְּלוּ־מָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: He sends out his word, and melts them; he makes his wind blow, and the waters flow.

notes.official: *yaššēb rûḥô yizzĕlû-māyim* 'he makes his wind blow, and the waters flow': *rûaḥ* is the wind that brings the thaw (`ruach-wind-breath-spirit-writings`).

paragraphs.text: מַגִּ֣יד דברו [דְּבָרָ֣יו] לְיַעֲקֹ֑ב חֻקָּ֥יו וּ֝מִשְׁפָּטָ֗יו לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: He declares his words to Jacob, his statutes and his ordinances to Israel.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *dbrw* 'his word' (singular) / Qere *dĕbārāyw* 'his words'. The Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-writings`); the ASV ('his word') follows the Ketiv. *ḥuqqāyw ûmišpāṭāyw* 'his statutes and his ordinances'. Jacob and Israel are in their English forms (`proper-names-english-forms-convention-writings`).

paragraphs.text: לֹ֘א עָ֤שָׂה כֵ֨ן ׀ לְכָל־גּ֗וֹי וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֥ים בַּל־יְדָע֗וּם הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: He has not done so for any nation, and as for his ordinances, they have not known them. Praise Yah!

notes.official: *ûmišpāṭîm bal-yĕdāʿûm* 'and as for his ordinances, they have not known them': the MT has no suffix on *mišpāṭîm*, and the English 'his' resumes v 19. The LXX reads 'he did not make his ordinances known to them' (*hôdîʿām*); the MT is followed (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`). The closing *hallĕlû-yāh* 'Praise Yah!' answers v 1 (`divine-names-convention-writings`).
